source_text: Σέβειν δὲ δεῖν ἐγκελευόμεθα καὶ τιμᾶν τὸν [αὐτὸν καὶ] λόγον, σωτῆρά τε αὐτὸν καὶ ἡγεμόνα εἶναι πεισθέντες, καὶ δι᾿ αὐτοῦ τὸν πατέρα, οὐκ ἐν ἐξαιρέτοις ἡμέραις, ὥσπερ ἄλλοι τινές, ἀλλὰ συνεχῶς τὸν ὅλον βίον τοῦτο πράττοντες καὶ κατὰ πάντα τρόπον. ἀμέλει »τὸ γένος τὸ ἐκλεκτὸν« »ἑπτάκις τῆς ἡμέρας ᾔνεσά σοι« φησί, κατ᾿ ἐντολὴν δικαιούμενον. ὅθεν οὔτε ὡρισμένον τόπον * οὔτε ἐξαίρετον ἱερὸν οὐδὲ μὴν ἑορτάς τινας καὶ ἡμέρας ἀποτεταγμένας, ἀλλὰ τὸν πάντα βίον ὁ γνωστικὸς ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ, κἂν καθ᾿ ἑαυτὸν μόνος ὢν τυγχάνῃ καὶ ὅπου τινὰς ἂν τῶν ὁμοίως πεπιστευκότων ἔχῃ, τιμᾷ τὸν θεόν, τουτέστιν χάριν ὁμολογεῖ τῆς γνώσεως καὶ τῆς πολιτείας. εἰ δὲ ἡ παρουσία τινὸς ἀνδρὸς ἀγαθοῦ διὰ τὴν ἐντροπὴν καὶ τὴν αἰδῶ πρὸς τὸ κρεῖττον ἀεὶ σχηματίζει τὸν ἐντυγχάνοντα, πῶς οὐ μᾶλλον ὁ συμπαρὼν ἀεὶ διὰ τῆς γνώσεως καὶ τοῦ βίου καὶ τῆς εὐχαριστίας ἀδιαλείπτως τῷ θεῷ οὐκ εὐλόγως ἂν ἑαυτοῦ παρ᾿ ἕκαστα κρείττων εἴη εἰς πάντα καὶ τὰ ἔργα καὶ τοὺς λόγους καὶ τὴν διάθεσιν; τοιοῦτος ὁ πάντῃ παρεῖναι τὸν θεὸν πεπεισμένος, οὐχὶ δὲ ἐν τόποις τισὶν ὡρισμένοις κατακεκλεισμένον ὑπολαβών, ἵνα δὴ χωρὶς αὐτοῦ ποτε οἰηθεὶς εἶναι καὶ νύκτωρ καὶ μεθ᾿ ἡμέραν ἀκολασταίνῃ. πάντα τοίνυν τὸν βίον ἑορτὴν ἄγοντες, πάντῃ πάντοθεν παρεῖναι τὸν θεὸν πεπεισμένοι, γεωργοῦμεν αἰνοῦντες, πλέομεν ὑμνοῦντες. κατὰ τὴν ἄλλην πολιτείαν ἐντέχνως ἀναστρεφόμεθα. προσεχέστερον δὲ ὁ γνωστικὸς οἰκειοῦται θεῷ σεμνὸς ὢν ἅμα καὶ ἱλαρὸς ἐν πᾶσι. σεμνὸς μὲν διὰ τὴν ἐπὶ τὸ θεῖον ἐπιστροφήν. ἱλαρὸς δὲ διὰ τὸν ἐπιλογισμὸν τῶν ἀνθρωπείων ἀγαθῶν ὧν ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν ὁ θεός. Φαίνεται δὲ τὸ ἔξοχον τῆς γνώσεως ὁ προφήτης ὧδε παριστάς· »χρηστότητα καὶ παιδείαν καὶ γνῶσιν δίδαξόν με·« κατ᾿ ἐπανάβασιν αὐξήσας τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν τῆς τελειότητος. οὗτος ἄρα ὄντως ὁ βασιλικὸς ἄνθρωπος, οὗτος ἱερεὺς ὅσιος τοῦ θεοῦ. ὅπερ ἔτι καὶ νῦν παρὰ τοῖς λογιωτάτοις τῶν βαρβάρων σῴζεται τὸ ἱερατικὸν γένος εἰς βασιλείαν προσαγόντων. οὗτος οὖν οὐδαμῇ μὲν ἑαυτὸν εἰς ὀχλοκρασίαν τὴν τῶν θεάτρων δεσπότιν ἐνδίδωσιν. τὰ λεγόμενα δὲ καὶ πραττόμενα καὶ ὁρώμενα ἡδονῆς ἀσώτου χάριν οὐδὲ ὄναρ προσίεται· οὔτ᾿ οὖν ταύτας τὰς ἡδονὰς τῆς θέας οὔτε τὰς διὰ τῶν ἄλλων ἀπολαυσμάτων ποικιλίας, οἷον θυμιαμάτων πολυτέλειαν τὴν ὄσφρησιν γοητεύουσαν ἢ βρωμάτων συγκαττύσεις καὶ τὰς ἐξ οἴνων διαφόρων ἀπολαύσεις δελεαζούσας τὴν γεῦσιν, οὐδὲ τὰς πολυανθεῖς καὶ εὐώδεις πλοκὰς ἐκθηλυνούσας δι᾿ αἰσθήσεως τὴν ψυχήν· πάντων δὲ τὴν σεμνὴν ἀπόλαυσιν ἐπὶ τὸν θεὸν ἀναγαγὼν ἀεὶ καὶ τῆς βρώσεως καὶ τοῦ πόματος καὶ τοῦ χρίσματος τῷ δοτῆρι τῶν ὅλων ἀπάρχεται, χάριν ὁμολογῶν καὶ [διὰ] τῆς δωρεᾶς καὶ τῆς χρήσεως διὰ λόγου τοῦ δοθέντος αὐτῷ.
pass_a_gloss: We are commanded to reverence and honor the Word, who is our Savior and Leader, and through Him, the Father, not just on special days, like others, but continuously throughout our entire life in every way. For the chosen race is justified, saying 'I have praised you seven times a day', and this is in accordance with the commandment. Therefore, the knowledgeable person does not need a specific place or a special temple or designated festivals and days, but rather honors God in every place and at all times, even when alone or with others who have similar faith. If the presence of a good man always shapes the one who encounters him to be better due to shame and respect, how much more will the one who is always present with God through knowledge and life and unceasing gratitude be better in all things, including deeds and words and disposition? The one who is convinced that God is present everywhere does not think that God is confined to specific places, so that he might sometimes think he is without God and behave recklessly day and night. Thus, we live our entire life as a festival, convinced that God is present everywhere, and we work while praising and sail while hymning. We live our life skillfully according to the rest of our civic duty. The knowledgeable person is more closely connected to God, being dignified and cheerful at the same time in all things. He is dignified because of his focus on the divine, and cheerful because of the calculation of human goods that God has given us. The prophet shows the excellence of knowledge, saying 'Teach me goodness and discipline and knowledge', increasing the ruling part of perfection. This, then, is truly the royal person, this is the holy priest of God, which is still preserved among the most reasonable of the barbarians, who bring the priestly race to the kingdom. This person does not give himself over to the dominion of the mob in the theaters. He does not even approach the things said and done and seen for the sake of intemperate pleasure, not even in a dream. He does not approach those pleasures of sight or the varied enjoyments through other senses, such as the expensive fragrance of incense deceiving the sense of smell or the agreements of foods and the different enjoyments of wine deceiving the sense of taste, or the many-colored and fragrant fabrics softening the soul through sensation. Rather, he always brings the dignified enjoyment of all things to God, and he offers gratitude to the Giver of all things for food and drink and anointing, acknowledging the gift and the use of the thing given to him through the word.

bible_refs.note: seven times a day I praise you

pass_b_english: We are commanded to reverence and honor the Word, for we have been persuaded that he is both Savior and Leader, and through him the Father as well; we must do this not only on special days, as some people do, but continuously throughout our entire life and in every possible way. For the chosen race is justified in saying, 'I have praised you seven times a day' (Psalm 119:164), doing so in accordance with the commandment. Therefore the knowledgeable person needs neither a designated place, nor a special temple, nor appointed festivals and days; rather, he honors God in every place and at all times, whether he happens to be alone or among others who believe likewise, which is to say he gives thanks for the knowledge and the way of life he has received. If the presence of a good man always molds the one who meets him toward what is better through shame and respect, how much more will the one who is continually present with God through knowledge, life, and unceasing gratitude become better in every respect — in deeds, words, and disposition? Such a person is convinced that God is present everywhere; he does not suppose that God is confined to specific places, lest he ever imagine himself to be without God and behave recklessly by day and by night. Consequently we conduct our whole life as a festival, persuaded that God is present everywhere; we farm while praising, we sail while singing hymns. We conduct ourselves skillfully according to the rest of our civic duty. The knowledgeable person draws especially near to God, being at once dignified and cheerful in all things: dignified because of his turning toward the divine, and cheerful because of his reckoning of the human goods that God has given us. The prophet displays the excellence of knowledge in these words: 'Teach me goodness, discipline, and knowledge,' increasing the ruling part of perfection. This one, then, is truly the royal man; this one is the holy priest of God — a priestly race still preserved even now among the most reasonable of the barbarians, who bring the priesthood to the kingdom. Such a man does not surrender himself to the rule of the mob in the theaters; he does not so much as approach in a dream the things said, done, and seen for the sake of dissolute pleasure. He avoids those pleasures of spectacle, and he avoids the varied enjoyments through the other senses — such as the costly fragrance of incense that beguiles the sense of smell, or the elaborate preparations of foods and the diverse enjoyments of wines that entice the sense of taste, or the many-hued and sweet-scented weaves that soften the soul through sensation. Instead, he always directs the dignified enjoyment of all things toward God, and for food and drink and anointing he offers first-fruits of thanksgiving to the Giver of all, acknowledging both the gift and the use of what was given to him through the Word.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A provides a faithful rendering of the clauses, and Pass B provides a more polished version that includes the required scripture citation (Psalm 119:164) for the quote 'I have praised you seven times a day' (corresponding to ἑπτάκις τῆς ἡμέρας ᾔνεσά σοι). All nuances regarding the 'knowledgeable person' (γνωστικὸς) and the distinction between dignity and cheerfulness are preserved.
